file_roles.evidence: Adds Item::locale_from_val_str(), the locale lookup moved out of Item_func_format::get_locale so the new 3-arg date_format can share it.
Declares locale_from_val_str() and a forward class MY_LOCALE; supports the helper move.
Removes Create_func_date_format and the DATE_FORMAT registry entry and switches callers to Item_func_date_format(thd, a, b) / Item_func_time_format; plumbing for the parser-level function.
Item_func_format::get_locale removed in favour of args[2]->locale_from_val_str(); same behaviour, relocated.
Drops get_locale declaration and makes locale const MY_LOCALE*; follows the helper move.

fix_length_and_dec and val_str now take the locale from args[2] when arg_count>=3 (locale_from_val_str), and eq() compares arg_count and args[2]; this makes the 3-arg form explicit-locale and deterministic.

check_vcol_func_processor changed from 'if (is_time_format) return false' to 'if (arg_count > 2) return false', so the generated-column check (the source of ERROR 1901) now accepts DATE_FORMAT with an explicit locale; also adds the 3-arg constructor and Item_func_time_format.
Adds the DATE_FORMAT keyword symbol so DATE_FORMAT can be parsed with special grammar for 2 and 3 args.
Adds DATE_FORMAT_SYM grammar rules for 2 and 3 arguments, plus a typo fix in a comment; syntax plumbing.
Same DATE_FORMAT_SYM grammar rules and comment typo fix for the Oracle-mode parser.

rationale: The reported error 1901 comes from the generated-column check, which rejects the 2-arg DATE_FORMAT because it depends on the session locale. The fix does not relax that check for the 2-arg form; it adds a 3-arg form with an explicit locale that is allowed. So this is closer to a new feature than a correction of wrong logic, and the old rejection may have been intended. I marked the evaluation and vcol-check code causal and the parser plumbing refactor, with low confidence.
notes: A maintainer statement that the 2-arg rejection was intentional would move item_timefunc files toward unclear or preventive.
